chunks.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحَكَمِ، عَنْ قُتَيْبَةَ الْعَشَاءِ قَالَ

translations.en: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Qutayba al-A'sha who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: عَادَيْتُمْ فِينَا الْآبَاءَ وَالْأَبْنَاءَ وَالْأَزْوَاجَ وَثَوَابُكُمْ عَلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ أَمَا إِنَّ أَحْرَجَ مَا تَكُونُونَ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ الْأَنفُسُ إِلَى هَذِهِ - وَأَشَارَ بِيَدِهِ إِلَى حَلْقِهِ

translations.en: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: You have made enemies of your fathers, sons, and wives because of us, and your reward is upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Verily, the most critical moment you will be in is when the souls reach here – and he pointed with his hand to his throat.

en.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the social cost of *al-wala'* (alliance) with the Ahl al-Bayt, where believers often face alienation from their non-Shia kin, yet assures them that their ultimate recompense rests with Allah. He emphasizes the critical moment of death (*al-hadd*) by gesturing to the throat, symbolizing the point where worldly ties are severed and the individual stands alone before God, underscoring the urgency of steadfastness in faith during life's trials.
en.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the relationship between Shia and their non-Shia families?
